scope: Disposable PostgreSQL 17.6 and PostgREST v14.18 only. The function was created for the proof and dropped before the database stopped. No Production DDL, grant, index, merge, deploy, or application activation.

runtime.postgrestPin: Current supabase/supabase docker-compose.yml rest image postgrest/postgrest:v14.18. Not a live project query.
runtime.statementTimeout: 0 on this disposable server. Comparison budget is the known 3000 ms production statement timeout.
runtime.collationNote: Windows ICU. This is not the Linux en_US.UTF-8 collation proof.

apiSyntax.resource: /providers on PostgREST. supabase-js sends the same order parameter on /rest/v1/providers.
apiSyntax.openapiNote: The v14.18 root document lists the 17 stored columns and RPCs. It does not list provider_name_nfc. Explicit select and order still resolve the field, and select=* omits it.

security.policy: Public can view verified providers USING (verified = true) for anon and authenticated

negativeControl.idForce: Applied only for this control, because the stored ids put the raw-first combining form on the smaller id. Original ids were restored.

multiCounty.method: Per-county API streams merged with compareFloridaHubOrderByNfc. No multi-county OR or ANY.

apiCostMs.note: Local disposable timings, not Supabase latency. Anon still sorts. No expression index was created.

publicationCompatibility.note: The function is name-only and stores nothing. Ordering the existing publication predicate did not change its row set. Publication-column writers, the publication index, and the publication-column app switch stay separate Founder GOs. Equal Osceola counts on this synthetic fixture are not a new eligibility predicate.

rollout: This disposable proof is complete. It does not authorize Production.

Smallest remaining GO: create public.provider_name_nfc(public.providers), revoke execute from PUBLIC, and grant execute to anon, authenticated, and service_role. No index, generated column, view, collation change, or application edit in that GO.

After that function is confirmed in the exposed Production schema, a separate GO switches both sides together: .order('provider_name_nfc').order('id') and compareFloridaHubOrder uses name.normalize('NFC').
Before the application switch, rollback is DROP FUNCTION public.provider_name_nfc(public.providers).
After the application switch, revert the application first. Dropping the function while the hub orders by it fails the read.
Do not combine this function with publication DDL, writer deploy, backfill, VALIDATE, the publication index, table-privilege revoke, or Production Packet 1 or Packet 2.
